# KiteConfig 2.1.0

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("io.github.yuroyami.kiteconfig") version "2.1.0"
}
```

A debug build can now have its own app id, name and icon, so it installs next
to the released app instead of replacing it:

```kotlin
kiteConfig {
    appId = "com.example.jetzy"
    debug {
        appId { suffix = ".debug" }
        appName = "Jetzy Dev"
        logo { background = color("#B00020") }
    }
}
```

Android applies it to the `debug` build type: the id suffix, the label, and
launcher icons generated into `build/` for the debug variants only. iOS applies
it to the `Debug` configuration of the target you already have: bundle id,
product name and icon set name, plus an `AppIcon-Debug.appiconset` next to the
release catalog. No new scheme and no new target. Turn the debug icon off and
the next apply takes the catalog back out.

`android { debug { } }` and `ios { debug { } }` hold what differs on one
platform, and name which build types or configurations count as debug.

Also new: `logo { overlay }` draws a PNG over the mark on every platform, which
is how you make a debug ribbon. `kiteConfig.debugAppIdFor(platform)` and
`debugAppNameFor(platform)` read the debug values back. `kiteVerify`,
`kitePlan` and `kiteDoctor` (`KTCNFG021`, `KTCNFG025`) know about the debug
build.

Only additions to the public API. Nothing that existed changed shape.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/yuroyami/KiteConfig/compare/v2.0.1...v2.1.0
